Course materials for the spring 2026 instance of *Introduction to Bioinformatics and Genome Analysis* (course code **5MO115**) at Umeå University.

Every exercise page has collapsible **Hint** and **Solution** callouts, plus an *Extra exercise material* section at the bottom for additional practice.

## Module 1 — R and basics

R is the workhorse of statistical bioinformatics. Module 1 covers the language from scratch (variables, types, vectors, matrices, data frames, control flow, reading data, plotting) and revisits the linear algebra and probability foundations needed for the rest of the course.

- [Lecture series — intro to R](module1/lectures/intro_R/0_R_syllabus.html) (14 short decks)
- Exercises: [linear algebra](module1/exercises/linalg/linalg.html) · [probability & Markov chains](module1/exercises/basicprob/basicprob.html) · [variables](module1/exercises/intro_R/creating_variables.html) · [data structures](module1/exercises/intro_R/complex_data_structures.html) · [reading & plotting](module1/exercises/intro_R/read_and_plot_data.html) · [control flow](module1/exercises/intro_R/loops_ifelse_functions.html)

## Module 2 — Command line

Most bioinformatics tools live on the command line. Module 2 covers Linux navigation, pipes, redirection, manipulating GTFs with `grep`/`awk`/`cut`, and running programs on a cluster.

- [Setup](module2/instructions/set_up_wsl.html) (Windows users: WSL; everyone else: R/RStudio + optional HPC2N access)
- [Lecture series — command line](module2/lectures/command_line/0_linux_syllabus.html)
- Exercises: [exploring the command line](module2/exercises/command_line/exploring_the_commandline.html) · [GTF files](module2/exercises/command_line/gtf.html) · [running programs](module2/exercises/command_line/running_programs.html) · [storing & accessing data](module2/exercises/command_line/storing_accessing_cmd.html)

## Module 3 — Genome data analysis

A pathogen-genome walkthrough from raw Illumina reads to a phylogenetic tree: quality control, de novo assembly, annotation, read mapping with variant calling, and tree building. Most exercises run on the HPC2N cluster.

- Lectures: [Intro](module3/lectures/intro.html) · [3.1a Quality control](module3/lectures/3_1a_quality_control.html) · [3.1b De novo assembly](module3/lectures/3_1b_de_novo_assembly.html) · [3.2 Annotation I](module3/lectures/3_2_annotation_part1.html) · [3.3 Annotation II](module3/lectures/3_3_annotation_part2.html) · [3.4 Read mapping & variants](module3/lectures/3_4_read_mapping.html) · [3.5 Phylogeny](module3/lectures/3_5_phylogeny.html)
- Exercises: [3.1 Quality control with fastp](module3/exercises/3_1_qc_fastp.html) · [3.1b De novo assembly](module3/exercises/3_1b_de_novo_assembly.html) · [3.3 Annotation](module3/exercises/3_3_annotation.html) · [3.4 SNP calling](module3/exercises/3_4_snp_calling.html) · [3.5 Phylogeny](module3/exercises/3_5_phylogeny.html)

## Module 4 — Statistics and RNA-seq

Where everything comes together: classical statistical distributions, simulation and bootstrap, linear models (`lm` and Stan), and a hands-on RNA-seq differential expression analysis from FASTQ to volcano plot.

- [Module 4 introduction](module4/intro.html)
- [4.1 — Basic statistics](module4/4_1_basic_stats.html)
- [4.2 — Simulations and bootstrapping](module4/4_2_sim_bootstrap.html)
- [4.3 — Linear models for statistics](module4/4_3_linmod.html)
- [4.4 — RNA-seq analysis](module4/4_4_rnaseq.html)
